what.label: supported
what.says: Plaka is the old neighbourhood on the north and east slopes of the Acropolis, with maze-like streets and neoclassical houses.
quote: is the old historical neighborhood of Athens, clustered around the northern and eastern slopes of the Acropolis, and incorporating labyrinthine streets and neoclassical architecture

gods.label: supported
gods.says: It is nicknamed the Neighbourhood of the Gods.
quote: It is known as the "Neighborhood of the Gods"

oldest.label: supported
oldest.says: It is the oldest district of Athens, lived in continuously since the Neolithic.
quote: It is the oldest district of Athens and has been continuously inhabited from the Neolithic to the present day.

streets.label: supported
streets.says: Some streets, such as Adrianou and Tripodon, go back to ancient times.
quote: Some of the streets, such as Adrianou and Tripodon, can be traced back to the ancient era.

name.label: disputed
name.says: The origin of the name Plaka is debated: perhaps "old Athens" in Arvanitika, or a plaque that once marked a crossroads.
quote: Some have suggested that the toponym Plaka derives from the Arvanitika Pliak Athena
Others have suggested that it derives from the presence of a plaque

albanian.label: supported
albanian.says: Plaka had a sizable Albanian community until the late 19th century.
quote: It had a sizable Albanian community until the late 19th century

fire.label: supported
fire.says: In 1884 a fire burned much of the neighbourhood, opening the way for excavations.
quote: In 1884, a fire burned down a large part of the neighborhood which gave the opportunity for the archaeologists to conduct excavations in the Roman Agora and Hadrian's Library.

underground.label: supported
underground.says: All utilities run in underground tunnels; it is the only Athens neighbourhood like that.
quote: as the only neighborhood in Athens where all utilities (water, power, cable television, telephone, internet, and sewage) lie underground

1826.label: supported
1826.says: Plaka was temporarily abandoned because of battles in 1826, and repopulated under King Otto.
quote: was temporarily abandoned by its inhabitants because of the severe battles that took place in 1826
The area was repopulated during the first years of the reign of Otto of Greece.

anafi.label: supported
anafi.says: Anafiotika was first built in King Otto's time by workers from the island of Anafi who came to work on the palace.
quote: The first houses were built in the era of Otto of Greece, when workers from the island of Anafi came to Athens in order to work as construction workers in the refurbishment of King Otto's Palace.

houses.label: supported
houses.says: Only 45 houses remain; streets are unnamed and houses go by numbers like "Anafiotika 1".
quote: there are only 45 houses remaining, while the little streets from Stratonos to the Acropolis rock are still unnamed
the houses are referred to as "Anafiotika 1"

style.label: supported
style.says: It was built in Cycladic style: small white cubic houses, steps and dead ends.
quote: The neighborhood was built according to typical Cycladic architecture
Houses are small and mostly cubic, small streets that often end up to ladders or even deadends at terraces

refugees.label: supported
refugees.says: Refugees from Asia Minor settled here in 1922.
quote: In 1922, Greek refugees from Asia Minor also established here

parts.name: Plaka
parts.stand: On Adrianou Street, any spot where you can see the Acropolis rock above the rooftops.

paras.t: This is Plaka, the old neighbourhood wrapped around the slopes below the Acropolis. People call it the Neighbourhood of the Gods. It's the oldest district in Athens, with people living here since the Stone Age. Even so, it was briefly emptied during the battles of 1826, in the War of Independence.
You're walking on very old lines. Some of these streets, this one, Adrianou, among them, follow routes that go back to ancient times.

Even the name is a small mystery. Some say Plaka comes from words meaning old Athens in the language of Albanian settlers, who lived here in large numbers until the late 1800s. Others say it's from a stone plaque that once marked a crossroads. Nobody knows for sure.
In 1884 a fire burned a large part of the neighbourhood. Archaeologists used the gap to dig at the Roman Agora and Hadrian's Library.
One more detail. According to the encyclopedia, Plaka's power, water and phone lines all run in tunnels underground, and it's the only Athens neighbourhood done that way.

parts.name: Anafiotika
parts.stand: From Stratonos Street, take the narrow lanes up toward the Acropolis rock. The steps are steep and uneven.

paras.t: Suddenly you're on a Greek island. This is Anafiotika. In the time of King Otto, builders from the island of Anafi came to work on the new royal palace, and they built themselves homes here the way they did back home.
Small white cube houses, steps that end at little terraces, and dead ends everywhere. Refugees from Asia Minor joined them in 1922.
Only 45 houses are left. The lanes have no names, and the houses go by numbers.
People live in these houses, so keep your voice down.
Find a terrace, look out over the city, and catch your breath. This is one of the quietest corners in the centre of Athens.
